outcome: A credible, researched, financially sound, executable plan that satisfies the owner's original objective inside every stated limit, graded USABLE by an independent grader.

dimensions.R: Does the result reach every component that needs it?
dimensions.I: Does the result change later decisions correctly?

RC1.name: Model turn is not checked before it counts
RC1.wrong: A model turn is not checked before it counts. Two distinct mechanisms: (a) HTTP 524 after ~125 s — the GPU pod proxy closes a non-streamed connection idle for 100 s (exam pass 2: streaming served every one); (b) content "" with no error in 47–85 s — the output budget (2,500–4,000 tokens) is spent on hidden reasoning (RC16). An empty reply was never treated as a failed turn.
RC1.proof: Replay: on the same prompts, empty replies retried with a larger budget answer; production route asks record zero empty-reply fall-throughs.
RC1.evidence: 30Q test: gpt-oss empty on 6/12 route asks; 524 at ~125 s on 2/3 question asks; integration diagnosis: 4/8 primary failures.

RC2.name: Critic veto is unchecked
RC2.wrong: The critic may drop any route on an assertion nothing verifies (date arithmetic, payment windows, fees the route never uses). Its word is final; when it drops all routes the owner gets no plan, even though the code can check most of what it asserts.
RC2.proof: Re-run the logged critiques: a drop resting on a false window/fee/capital claim is overruled by the deterministic check; outputs with zero surviving routes fall from 9/12.
RC2.evidence: 30Q: critic dropped 14 of 18 parsed routes; >=4 on misreadings (net-30 outside 60 days; Dec 3-7 after a Feb window; a $5 fee not used; service agreement as payment risk). Integration diagnosis: 6/8 asks ended empty, p10 false WINDOW x3. | REVIEW 3: most cited misreadings were written by the fallback (laguna, 1/30) critiquing its own routes after one primary failure; the code-level veto weakness is real but secondary.

RC3.name: A standing operating rule is presented as the owner's own constraint
RC3.wrong: Brain's operating-model sentence and REMOTE_AI_FOCUS are injected into goal prompts beside the owner's limits; models copy them into the owner's refusals and discovery searches online-only work for owners who offered labour or own equipment. The goal-specific lift exists only in the route prompt and only when a regex matches. REVIEW 3 + fresh batch: the lift reached none of the prompts actually sent — every final 30Q prompt, the strong control's included, carried "run entirely online" for owners offering work; the phrase reader missed 14 of 30 fresh owners who stated hours.
RC3.proof: Owner profiles in replies carry no refusal the owner did not state; discovery questions for an owner with stated labour/equipment are not online-only.
RC3.evidence: Integration diagnosis: 4/4 fallback replies invented refusals; 30Q p02 run 1 owner profile "no physical work" for a drone pilot. Partly repaired d5beaf6 (route prompt); discovery unchanged (code).

RC4.name: Verified findings are lost on the way to the planner
RC4.wrong: The proposer is shown at most 40 findings, newest first, with near-duplicates judged on the first 160 characters; refuted claims are not filtered; nothing selects findings by the decision they bear on.
RC4.proof: With all verified findings available, the planner's input holds every distinct verified finding (or a relevance-chosen set that covers every ground field), and a refuted claim is never shown.
RC4.evidence: 30Q: 40 of 111/111/135 delivered under the cap; uncapped near-dup filter dropped 6 and 9; graders attribute 3/12 failures to C. Code: refuted not filtered.

RC5.name: Inquiry and direction-finding anchor on one menu
RC5.wrong: Question generation and scouting fix on a business shape before research (brokered digital tasks, dropshipping) and never ask whether the owner can be paid directly for what they can do now; follow-ups narrow onto the same shape.
RC5.owner: routeProposal.ts directionPrompt (and the questions framing that reuses it); discovery lenses
RC5.proof: Fresh goals: the question set and directions include the owner's direct means and at least three structurally different mechanisms; p06-type goals surface direct paid work.
RC5.evidence: 30Q: p06 60 questions all brokerage/digital; p10 60 questions dropshipping/ad-services; graders: strongest p06 path (owner as Tasker) found by no output. | REVIEW 3: the anchoring questions were written under a LIMITS block carrying the standing online-only rule.

RC6.wrong: Fragments are not executed, 69% of searches are refused, no keyed search provider is configured, Firecrawl is held to 15 credits/day, and the read-capable routine workers are not members of evaluation projects.
RC6.owner: research coordinator/queue; server/services/sources/*; owner items (keyed search key)
RC6.proof: A fresh goal's research completes its planned fragments and its plan reads >=20 relevant verified facts within the goal window.
RC6.evidence: RESEARCH-STARVATION-DIAGNOSIS: 1/16 fragments completed; 30Q traces: 0/1/0 completions after ~6 h; searches 785/1142 refused. Operator capacity 06:20-07:00Z (RC6 owner session_01QF5Tk5NBNTchKMwPJPQFEc): about 20 research fragments SUCCEEDED per hour Brain-wide; the GPU lane is held below its slot target (inFlight 3 of 8) by "database connections contended"; each restart holds the free lane at START_TARGET=2 for 10 min and resumes at half the saved target (16 restarts/24h, about 160 min/day); fragmentSearchRoom is 2 Brain-wide once Firecrawl hits its ceiling (34 CEILING vs 7 ANSWERED/24h; DDG 817 refused vs 416 answered). The free-lane database-saturation brake fired 253 times/24h while checkouts waited 0 ms p95, a false brake, corrected by #1342 (queue session). RC7.name: No shared per-goal working state
RC7.wrong: Each faculty writes its conclusions to its own store; the next faculty re-derives or never reads them (rethink and calibration lessons, owner profile, committee questions, plan verdict and binding factor are not inputs to the route ask).
RC7.proof: A route ask's context shows the previous ask's rethink, the plan verdict and binding factor, and open committee questions; a lesson recorded once changes the next ask.
RC7.evidence: Integration diagnosis §2 "present but unused" (code and production).

RC8.name: Route economics are left to the model
RC8.kind: SYMPTOM of RC17/RC14 (code check is the safeguard)
RC8.wrong: Nothing computes, before a route counts, whether its price x realistic volume reaches the target, whether paid acquisition at the cited cost per sale fits the capital, or whether the buyer count supports the sales needed; models get the arithmetic wrong in both directions (proposer optimistic, critic pessimistic).
RC8.proof: Logged routes: the 445-sales-from-$3k beanie route is flagged by code; a sound route is not. The critic sees the computed figures.
RC8.evidence: 30Q graders: p10 beanie routes (445 sales from $3,000 at $39 CPA), p02 critic multiplying CPL by an inflated buyer count, p06 invented $10/h subcontractor. | REVIEW 3: every concrete instance came from the fallback model.

RC12.kind: CONTRADICTED as a cause of unusable plans (graders judged content, not acceptance state); kept as a readiness-signal defect
RC12.wrong: Plan acceptance needs every input evidenced at sample>=20 and p5 reach>=90%; research alone cannot move it, so "ready" is never signalled by a research-backed plan.

RC13.name: The owner's plan is built from generic constructed arrangements that never read the owner
RC13.wrong: Until route openings exist, readGoalPlan models the arrangement constructor's generic designs (fractional aircraft ownership, HVAC referral brokering) for every goal; the constructor and its research steps never read the owner's words, means or place, so the plan the owner is handed fits any request.

RC15.wrong: The regex reader has no reading for several ordinary ways people state a window, a spending cap, an hours rate or no time at all, so a goal is refused or carries a wrong limit into every later step.

RC16.name: Output budgets too small for a reasoning model
RC16.wrong: Route, critique and direction asks gave gpt-oss-120b 2,500–4,000 max_tokens; hidden reasoning consumed them and the reply arrived empty or cut mid-JSON.
RC16.proof: Production route asks show no empty or truncated primary replies; exam at 16,000 had 0/47 empty.
RC16.evidence: Root-cause challenge: empty replies in 47–85 s with error:null (planner/final_*.txt, probe1_*.txt); question replies cut mid-JSON (questions/*.raw.txt).

RC17.name: Model fall-through has no competence floor; the proposer critiques itself
RC17.wrong: After one primary failure the fallback combo (laguna-xs-2.1: 1/30, 0/11 planning, 19 critical errors) both proposed and critiqued; the critic order puts the proposing model first, so the check is not independent.
RC17.proof: No route ask is answered or critiqued by a model below the planning bar; production route events show the fallback never serves.
RC17.evidence: Root-cause challenge: 6 of 12 probes and 2 of 3 question sets served by the fallback; routeProposal.ts "The model that proposed critiques first".

RC18.name: The evaluation was underpowered and its grading standard drifted
RC18.wrong: Three goals, one sample per arm, one grader per goal whose bar moved between days; the rubric had no cause categories separating model, research capacity, timing and code.
RC18.proof: 30 fresh goals on one frozen revision, graded blind with a fixed rubric that records a cause category per failure.
RC18.evidence: 30Q report: "Today's grader was stricter"; validity review on GRADING.md / GRADING-E2E.md.

RC19.name: A goal's research never starts: its ideas are not judged within the goal's window
RC19.wrong: The tick's judge pass judged at most 5 goal ideas a tick under database pressure, ticks run many minutes when dozens of goal plans are read in sequence (30–40 s each), and the goal-idea queue held ideas of cancelled and paused goals (matched by how they were made, never by whether their goal still runs) ahead of live goals'. 30 fresh goals produced 605 ideas; none was judged in 1.5 h, so no mission, fragment or claim existed and every plan stayed on generic constructed estimates.
RC19.proof: On a fresh batch, each live goal's first ideas are judged within one tick and its first research fragments are queued within the hour.
RC19.evidence: planningEval judging (08:00Z): run ideas 605 CAPTURED unjudged, head of the goal queue created 05:56–06:08Z by the retired fm1126a and paused goals, updated_at = created_at; judge-one: one judgment 1.75 s; judge-pass: the pass body judged 18 in 20 s — so the pass works and is starved by budget and queue, not broken.

RC20.wrong: goalPriceSql and goalRoundSql (goals/goalWork.ts) named ideas as goal work by how they were made, never by whether their goal still runs, so in nextLaunchable's order (fits, goal tier, per-project turn, tier) paused and ended goals' price questions (tier 0) and rounds (tier 1) stood ahead of a live goal's dives and ideas (tiers 2-3). A tick fills 5-30 launches inside a 30 s budget and ticks run ~17 min, so the head was refilled from other projects every tick. The packet runner's plan-read boost used the same ungated predicate.
RC20.owner: goals/goalWork.ts goalPriceSql, goalRoundSql (read by russell/loop.ts nextLaunchable and research/packetRunner.ts servesGoalPlanRead)
RC20.proof: On a fresh batch, each live goal's judged ideas launch missions within a tick or two of being judged, and its first fragments run within the hour.

capabilities.name: Read the objective (amount, currency, window, capital, hours, recurrence, place)
capabilities.why: Every limit a plan is judged against comes from this reading.

capabilities.name: Read the owner's means without inventing them (skills, assets, licences, location, authority, refusals)
capabilities.why: Owner fit is the first feasibility rule; invented refusals or skills send every route wrong.

capabilities.name: Resolve Brain's standing operating rule against the goal's own offer, once, as data
capabilities.why: Brain's rule and the owner's offer must not contradict each other in any prompt or gate.

capabilities.name: Keep one consistent understanding of the goal across faculties and time
capabilities.why: Plans built by faculties that disagree about the goal cannot be coherent.

capabilities.name: Calendar, season and window arithmetic
capabilities.why: Whether money settles inside the window decides feasibility.

capabilities.name: Know the local economic environment (buyers in the place, market conditions, season)
capabilities.why: Routes must target buyers who exist and are buying now, there.

capabilities.name: Discover opportunities without being given a strategy
capabilities.why: The plan can only be as good as the best opportunity considered.

capabilities.name: Generate genuinely different approaches
capabilities.why: Comparison needs real alternatives, not variations.

capabilities.name: Pre-screen against hard limits (capital, hours, window, lawful)
capabilities.why: Infeasible routes waste research and mislead.

capabilities.name: Identify what must be known before choosing (decisive unknowns)
capabilities.why: Research effort must go where an answer changes the decision.

capabilities.name: Ask useful, non-anchored research questions
capabilities.why: Questions decide what can ever be learned.

capabilities.name: Prioritise follow-ups and stop when research cannot change the decision
capabilities.why: Unbounded research wastes scarce capacity; premature stop leaves gaps.

capabilities.name: Search provider availability and capacity
capabilities.why: No search, no facts.

capabilities.name: Research work executes (fragments complete)
capabilities.why: Planned research must actually run.

capabilities.name: Open and read the pages
capabilities.why: Search snippets are not evidence.

capabilities.name: Extract claims with exact citations
capabilities.why: A planner can only cite what was extracted with its source.

capabilities.name: Verify that the evidence supports the claim
capabilities.why: Unverified claims mislead the planner.

capabilities.name: Type the evidence (what it establishes: lane, scope exact/comparable, place, date)
capabilities.why: A fact about another segment or another figure must not ground this one.

capabilities.name: Combine facts and detect contradictions
capabilities.why: Contradicted routes must be rejected; conflicting facts resolved.

capabilities.name: Knowledge library matching (buyer identity, counts)
capabilities.why: Wrong buyer counts close the buyer question falsely.

capabilities.name: Deliver verified findings into the proposer's reasoning input
capabilities.why: A fact not shown cannot change the plan.

capabilities.name: Deliver findings and conclusions to other faculties (constructor, committee, dives, report, operator)
capabilities.why: Every faculty that decides must see the evidence.

capabilities.name: A model turn returns a valid answer (no empty/timeout/unparseable fall-through)
capabilities.why: Every reasoning step depends on a model actually answering.

capabilities.name: Propose routes that use the evidence correctly
capabilities.why: The plan is built from these routes.

capabilities.name: Quantitative and causal economics (price x volume, CAC vs capital, margin, hours, reach)
capabilities.why: A plan is financially sound only if the arithmetic holds.

capabilities.name: Payment terms and time to collected cash
capabilities.why: Money must be collected, not pending, inside the window.

capabilities.name: Buyer discovery and acquisition channel reasoning
capabilities.why: Without a channel that produces buyers in time, no plan works.

capabilities.name: Fulfilment and subcontractor reasoning
capabilities.why: Someone named must deliver at a known cost.

capabilities.name: Legal and platform-terms reasoning
capabilities.why: Unlawful or ToS-breaking plans are not usable.

capabilities.name: Parser and mechanical validation (correct rejections; repair, not loss)
capabilities.why: Mechanical checks must remove bad routes without losing good ones.

capabilities.name: Criticise correctly (drop only on verified grounds)
capabilities.why: The critic has the last word on what the owner receives.

capabilities.name: Revise after critique (replacement routes)
capabilities.why: Criticism must improve the plan, not end it.

capabilities.name: Compare and select one strategy
capabilities.why: The owner needs one plan, chosen on evidence.

capabilities.name: Identify risks and invalid assumptions
capabilities.why: Unexamined assumptions sink plans.

capabilities.name: Know when a plan is ready (and when more research is needed)
capabilities.why: Neither premature nor never.

capabilities.name: Convert the chosen strategy into a complete executable plan
capabilities.why: A route is not a plan: steps, who, when, cost, first actions, acceptance.

capabilities.name: Learn from previous findings and failures
capabilities.why: The same mistake must not repeat.

capabilities.name: Adapt when circumstances change (owner change, new evidence, refutation)
capabilities.why: Plans must follow reality.

capabilities.name: Recover from model, research and software failures
capabilities.why: Failures are frequent; recovery must be automatic.

capabilities.name: Own the next step of every goal (no unowned step)
capabilities.why: Work nobody owns does not happen.

capabilities.name: Choose models by their measured results on this work
capabilities.why: The model that answers must be the one that reasons best here.

capabilities.name: Present a usable plan to the owner
capabilities.why: The owner must be able to act on it.

capabilities.name: Constructed arrangement generation and candidate selection (the non-LLM generator)
capabilities.why: goalArrangements feeds composeGoalModel; the arrangement set is the main supply of openings the planner and reconstruction can adopt. HELD slots keep last readings' leaders, so a bad early leader can lock out alternatives.
